facts.claim: NYS Clean Heat is one statewide heat pump program run through six utilities. Existing 1 to 4 unit homes (and 1 to 4 whole apartments in larger buildings) with an electric customer who pays the System Benefits Charge. Full-load systems only (at least 100% of the building heating load, Manual J required), cold-climate air-source heat pumps on the NEEP list, participating contractor. Version 3 of the manual took effect September 1, 2026 and added a Weatherized Tier with higher amounts for homes built after 2010, homes that took part in an approved weatherization program, or homes that pass a heating-load test.
facts.eligibility: Electric customers of the participating utility; 1-4 family homes; must use a NYS Clean Heat participating contractor; incentive is paid through the contractor and shown on the invoice.
facts.notes: Replaces the March 2026 version 2 figures. Many pages double-counted 'utility rebate + NYS Clean Heat'. That is the same money.

facts.claim: Incentives are limited to 70% of project cost, or 85% in a disadvantaged community or in Central Hudson territory.
facts.eligibility: All Clean Heat utilities
facts.notes: Rules out any 'rebate exceeds system cost' claim.

facts.claim: Single-family, non-DAC: Category 2a with integrated controls $2,500 (no Weatherized Tier); Category 2b with decommissioning $7,000, or $10,000 in the Weatherized Tier. DAC: 2a $4,500; 2b $8,000, or $11,000 in the Weatherized Tier. Apartments get about half. Partial to full load $4,000 single-family, $1,500 apartment. Applied as an instant discount by a participating contractor.
facts.eligibility: Con Edison electric customers in NYC and Westchester; participating contractor; home must be service adequate
facts.notes: Con Edison's own page says up to $11,000, which matches. Earlier fact said up to $10,000 ($11,000 DAC), from the March version 2.

facts.claim: Whole-building retrofit rates for geothermal: $25,000 non-DAC or $35,000 DAC, rising to $30,000 and $40,000 in the Weatherized Tier. New construction $15,000 per home outside a DAC and $20,000 inside. Scope must include every dwelling unit in the 1 to 4 unit building, and existing buildings must decommission the old heating system.
facts.eligibility: Scope must include all dwelling units in the 1-4 unit building

facts.claim: Single-family, non-DAC: Category 2 (no decommissioning) $4,000, or $8,000 in the Weatherized Tier; Category 2b with decommissioning $7,000, or $12,000. DAC: Category 2 $6,000 / $10,000; 2b $9,000 / $14,000. Apartments or homes under 1,000 sq ft get about half. Partial to full load $4,000. Geothermal retrofit $18,000 ($23,000 Wx) non-DAC, $23,000 ($28,000 Wx) DAC.
facts.eligibility: National Grid upstate electric customers; participating contractor
facts.notes: National Grid's electric heating page still says 'up to $12,000' for central and mini-split heat pumps on 2026-10-03, which is the pre-Weatherized-Tier figure. The manual is the program document.

facts.claim: Same table as NYSEG. Single-family, non-DAC: Category 2 $4,000 ($8,000 Weatherized Tier); 2b $7,000 ($12,000). DAC: Category 2 $5,000 ($9,000); 2b $8,000 ($13,000). Apartments about half. Partial to full load $3,000 ($1,500 apartment). Geothermal retrofit $15,000 ($20,000 Wx) non-DAC and $16,000 ($21,000) DAC.
facts.eligibility: RG&E electric customers. The City of Rochester is served by RG&E, NOT National Grid.
facts.notes: The City of Rochester is served by RG&E, not National Grid. Rochester pages sit under /us/ny/national-grid/rochester/ (URL can't change) but copy must name RG&E.

facts.claim: Single-family, non-DAC: Category 2 $4,000 ($8,000 Weatherized Tier); 2b $7,000 ($12,000). DAC: Category 2 $5,000 ($9,000); 2b $8,000 ($13,000). Apartments about half. Partial to full load $3,000 ($1,500 apartment). Geothermal retrofit $15,000 ($20,000 Wx) non-DAC and $16,000 ($21,000) DAC.
facts.eligibility: NYSEG electric customers
facts.notes: NYSEG's own page still says up to $10,000 for air-source and up to $18,000 for ground-source on 2026-10-03, the pre-September figures. The manual is the program document.

facts.claim: Single-family over 1,000 sq ft: Category 2 $4,000 ($8,000 Weatherized Tier); 2b with decommissioning $7,000 ($12,000); partial to full load $3,000. Apartment or home under 1,000 sq ft: $2,000 ($4,000), $3,500 ($6,000), $1,000. Geothermal retrofit $15,000 ($20,000 Wx), new construction $8,000. Central Hudson's page lists the same amounts. Incentives up to 85% of project cost.
facts.eligibility: Central Hudson electric customers (Poughkeepsie, Kingston, Newburgh, Beacon, Saugerties)
facts.notes: Matches cenhud.com's heat pump page read 2026-10-03. No separate DAC column.

facts.claim: Single-family, non-DAC: Category 2 $4,000 ($8,000 Weatherized Tier); 2b $7,000 ($12,000). DAC: Category 2 $6,000 ($10,000); 2b $9,000 ($14,000). Apartments about half. Partial to full load $4,000 ($2,000 apartment). Geothermal retrofit $18,000 ($23,000 Wx) non-DAC, $20,000 ($25,000) DAC.
facts.eligibility: O&R electric customers

facts.program: Clean Heat heat pump water heaters
facts.claim: Heat pump water heater: $1,250 upstate (Central Hudson, National Grid, NYSEG, O&R, RG&E) and $1,300 Con Edison through retail or midstream channels. Con Edison runs a limited-time offer at $1,500 for applications submitted September 1 to November 30, 2026, and NYSEG and RG&E raise the distributor and installer payments in the same window. Must meet ENERGY STAR with a UEF rating. A homeowner can apply directly and install their own unit if codes are followed; installers must be NYS licensed.
facts.eligibility: Electric customers of the utility
facts.dates: Manual version 3; limited-time offers September 1 to November 30, 2026

facts.program: PSEG Long Island heat pump rebates (not NYS Clean Heat)
facts.claim: Single-family whole-house projects: $7,500 low income (under 60% of area median income), $5,000 moderate income (under 80%) or market rate in a disadvantaged community, $4,000 market rate, plus $250 to the contractor. The heat pump must meet 100 to 120% of the whole-dwelling heating load with a Manual J, be on the NEEP cold-climate list, use integrated controls or remove fossil heat, and be installed by a participating contractor. 2026 income limits for a household of four: $98,925 low income, $131,900 moderate.
facts.eligibility: PSEG Long Island electric customers; NEEP-listed equipment; sized for the whole home; participating contractor; pre-approval before work starts
facts.notes: PSEG LI is run for LIPA and is NOT part of NYS Clean Heat. Read 2026-10-03.

facts.claim: Low-income single-family households: no-cost energy efficiency improvements capped at $12,000 upstate / $14,000 downstate. Moderate-income: 50% of cost capped at $6,000 upstate / $7,000 downstate. Sustainable Futures Program adds up to $5,000 for a heat pump water heater, $10,000 air source heat pump, $10,000 ground source, $5,000 panel box and $2,500 wiring. HEAR adds up to $1,600 for air sealing, insulation and ventilation. Downstate counties: Bronx, Dutchess, Nassau, New York, Orange, Putnam, Queens, Richmond, Rockland, Suffolk, Ulster, Westchester, Kings.
facts.eligibility: Income-eligible owners AND renters of 1-4 family homes; limits by county and household size
facts.notes: Federal IRA Home Energy Rebates (HER/HOMES and HEAR) money is delivered to 1-4 family homes THROUGH EmPower+ - homeowners do not apply to HEAR separately.

facts.program: IRA Home Energy Rebates in NY (HOMES/HER + HEAR)
facts.claim: NY's $317.4M allocation ($159M HER + $158.4M HEAR) is being rolled out for income-eligible households through EmPower+ and NYSERDA's Appliance Upgrade Program (retail rebates on heat pump clothes dryers). There is no standalone 'federal HEAR $4,000-$8,000' rebate any homeowner can add on top of a Clean Heat heat pump rebate.
facts.eligibility: Low income <80% AMI; moderate 80-150% AMI (DOE definitions)
facts.notes: Also https://www.nyserda.ny.gov/-/media/Project/Nyserda/Files/Programs/IRA/IRA-HER-HEAR-FAQ.pdf

facts.claim: Seal-and-insulate packages through Comfort Home contractors: Good (seal and insulate attic and rim joist) $2,500, Better (Good plus walls and floors) $3,000, ENERGY STAR windows add-on $2,000 after air sealing and insulation. A later package within a year can get $1,000 more, or $2,000 after more than a year. Starts with a no-fee contractor consultation; eligibility checked through a MyEnergy account; contractors listed by county.
facts.eligibility: Through Comfort Home contractors in participating counties
facts.dates: open status for 2026 not stated on page
facts.notes: Pages tell readers to confirm the county is covered.

facts.claim: Affordable Solar residential incentive (income-eligible): $0.80/W in Con Edison territory, $0.40/W on Long Island. Market-rate per-watt amounts change by block - check NYSERDA's regional dashboards.
facts.eligibility: Income-eligible for Affordable Solar
facts.notes: Market-rate $/W not verified - pages say 'check the current block'.

facts.claim: No hardware rebate for home chargers. Pays 10 cents/kWh for off-peak charging (midnight-8am), $25 bonus after 3 months, $35 per summer month / bonus for avoiding weekday 2-6pm charging Jun 1-Sep 30; about $400/year on average.
facts.eligibility: Charge in NYC or Westchester with a compatible EV or charger; not eligible if on Residential/Small Business TOU rate (SC1/SC2)

facts.claim: Stopped accepting new Level 2 applications as of April 22, 2026; DCFC paused.
facts.eligibility: Was for make-ready infrastructure at sites, not single-family home chargers
facts.dates: closed to new L2 apps April 22, 2026

facts.claim: Residential: 30% up to $1,000 per item, only for property placed in service by June 30, 2026.
facts.eligibility: n/a

facts.program: PSEG Long Island heat pump water heater
facts.claim: Rebates up to $1,200.
facts.eligibility: PSEG LI customers
facts.notes: Same page: smart thermostat $100-$130; Smart Savers $85 with central air.

facts.claim: Long Island: NYSERDA storage installation incentive only for grid-connected residential solar paired with a battery (new solar plus storage, or a battery added to existing solar). A participating NY-Sun contractor applies for it; it covers only the storage part. Extra incentives for households under 80% of area median income. Batteries can also earn payments in LIPA's Dynamic Load Management program at peak times.
facts.eligibility: Solar-paired
facts.notes: Old pages claimed '$200/kWh = $2,700' for PSEG; removed.

facts.claim: Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit (25C) and Residential Clean Energy Credit (25D) do not apply to property placed in service after December 31, 2025.
facts.eligibility: n/a
facts.notes: Per P.L. 119-21 (2025). Pages must not present them as available.

facts.claim: From September 1, 2026 higher heat pump amounts apply to homes that qualify through any one of three pathways: built after 2010; took part in an approved utility or NYSERDA weatherization program (Con Edison Weather Ready & Sealed, NYSEG/RG&E Home Insulation and Air Sealing, NYSERDA Comfort Home, National Grid Total Home Comfort, O&R Sealed Comfort Plan); or pass a heating-load test (Btu per hour per sq ft below a limit that depends on home size and territory). Con Edison pays no Weatherized Tier for projects with integrated controls. By March 1, 2028 the program must adopt weatherization as a prerequisite.
facts.eligibility: See claim
facts.notes: Read in manual version 3 on 2026-10-03; cleanheat.ny.gov says a significantly higher rebate is available for weatherized homes.

facts.program: National Grid Whole Home Electrification Program
facts.claim: By invitation only for a small number of customers in select upstate communities. May cover up to 100% of eligible electrification costs, with a free home energy assessment ($50 gift card) and a five-year monthly bill credit for customers who switch from gas to a heat pump. Customers who did not receive an invitation are not eligible.
facts.eligibility: Invited customers only

facts.claim: Con Edison says heat pump users can save an average of 10% by switching to its Steady Use Rate.
facts.eligibility: Con Edison customers with heat pumps
facts.notes: A utility claim, not independently checked.

facts.program: NYSERDA Residential Energy Storage Program (outside Long Island)
facts.claim: NYSERDA offers incentives for home batteries of 25 kWh or less that are new, permanent and stationary and installed by a participating contractor. The per-kWh rate varies by region and changes over time (residential incentive dashboard); NYSERDA says a project can generally receive several thousand dollars, more for income-eligible homes or a Disadvantaged Community. Long Island incentives go through PSEG Long Island instead.
facts.eligibility: Homes outside Long Island; battery 25 kWh or less; participating contractor
facts.notes: Dashboard rates are in an iframe and were not read; no dollar figure is stated on pages. Overview page: https://www.nyserda.ny.gov/All-Programs/Energy-Storage-Program/Energy-Storage-for-Your-Home

facts.claim: $85 rebate for enrolling an eligible Honeywell, Sensi, Alarm.com or Amazon smart thermostat; $25 per year retention incentive for taking part in 50% or more of event hours over the first three years. Requires central air conditioning; not combined with Smart Usage Rewards. Events are weekday adjustments to AC, May to September, 11 a.m. to 11 p.m.; rebate in 6 to 8 weeks.
facts.eligibility: Con Edison electric customers with central AC and an eligible thermostat
facts.notes: Smart Usage Rewards (any customer with a smart meter, rewards set by third-party partners, May 1 to Sep 30): https://www.coned.com/en/save-money/rebates-incentives-tax-credits/rebates-incentives-tax-credits-for-residential-customers/smart-usage-rewards

facts.program: Con Edison Weather Ready (insulation and air sealing)
facts.claim: No longer accepting applications. Con Edison points Westchester homes to NYSERDA's Comfort Home Program and says Residential Weatherization incentives for 2027 will be announced.
facts.eligibility: Was for 1 to 4 family homes heated by Con Edison gas or electricity, or delivered fuel with Con Edison electric cooling
facts.notes: Con Edison's residential page still showed 'up to $4,000' teaser text on 2026-10-03; the program page says closed.

facts.program: National Grid Weatherization Health and Safety Program (upstate NY)
facts.claim: No-cost home safety improvements for National Grid New York customers who meet EmPower+ income guidelines, in single-family homes or rentals of 4 units or less (renters need landlord approval). Only after applying to EmPower+ and completing a no-cost Health and Safety Assessment; pre-selected contractors; administered by CLEAResult.
facts.eligibility: EmPower+ income-eligible National Grid customers

facts.program: National Grid upstate gas rebates (HEHE) and midstream
facts.claim: National Grid's Gas Prescriptive Rebate (HEHE) program is no longer accepting applications, and in-store midstream rebates are no longer available.
facts.notes: Same site: heat pump water heater rebate up to $1,250 through NYS Clean Heat (https://www.nationalgridus.com/Upstate-NY-Home/Energy-Saving-Programs/Electric-Heat-Pump-Water-Heaters).

facts.program: NY-Sun incentive, NY solar tax credit and property tax exemption
facts.claim: NY-Sun incentives are given through a participating contractor, usually taken off the price, and must be disclosed in the contract; the amount depends on project size and location and phases down over time. Households under 80% of area median income may get more through Affordable Solar. New York State personal tax credit of 25% for panels at your residence. NYS Real Property Tax Exemption keeps added value off property taxes unless the local government opted out; New York City offers its own Real Property Tax Abatement instead. NYSERDA loans: On-Bill Recovery and Smart Energy Loans.
facts.amount: 25% state tax credit; NY-Sun per-watt varies
facts.eligibility: Homeowners using a NY-Sun contractor
facts.notes: State tax credit cap not stated on this page; do not state one.

facts.program: PSEG Long Island smart thermostat rebates
facts.claim: $100 or $130 rebate on eligible ENERGY STAR smart thermostats (not stacked with Marketplace purchases); $85 Smart Savers rebate with central air and a qualifying thermostat that allows short remote adjustments at peak times.
facts.eligibility: PSEG Long Island customers
